14 — GEO and AEO Checklist#

Improve how clearly and reliably a project can be understood, sourced, and answered by search answer systems and generative AI. GEO = Generative Engine Optimization; AEO = Answer Engine Optimization. Neither guarantees citation or inclusion.

Scope: Frontend-specific. This file is one part of the 14_GEO_and_AEO.md checklist. Apply the domain-wide release gate across all applicable scope files; each checklist ID remains unique.

Review ownership: The consolidated checklist is frontend-led for website content, answer quality, authority, and discovery; involve editorial, analytics, legal, and other cross-team reviewers for relevant checks. Related backend and AI domain files retain their specialized checks.

Review details#

  • Project / product:
  • Release / version / environment:
  • Scope and applicable jurisdictions / markets:
  • Reviewer / owner:
  • Review date:
  • Decision: Pending / Approved / Approved with documented exceptions / Blocked

How to use#

  1. Copy this template into each project's review records; keep the shared repository template unchecked.
  2. Check [x] only after verifying the item with evidence. For any inapplicable item, record N/A and the reason in the project's own review notes or issue tracker using its checklist ID; do not mark it as passed.
  3. Record evidence links or artifact references by checklist ID. Open an issue for every failed item, assign an owner and due date, and retest after remediation.
  4. Apply the release gate below. These checklists guide review; they do not replace qualified specialist review when required.

Audience, answer intent, and coverage#

  • GEO-001 High-value user questions, follow-ups, and conversational queries are inventoried.
  • GEO-002 Questions are mapped to authoritative, relevant pages with a clear intended answer.
  • GEO-003 Content distinguishes definitions, instructions, comparisons, FAQs, and decision criteria.
  • GEO-004 Answers reflect audience knowledge level and include scope, caveats, and applicability.
  • GEO-005 Important topics have sufficient depth and context beyond isolated keyword phrases.
  • GEO-037 Include legitimate comparison and follow-up questions without making redundant doorway pages.
  • GEO-038 Evaluate whether visitors can independently verify critical claims from the cited primary evidence.
  • GEO-039 Identify authoritative, public canonical pages for each product, concept, service, or policy.

Answer-ready structure and clarity#

  • GEO-006 Priority pages state a concise, accurate answer close to the related question or heading.
  • GEO-007 Headings, short paragraphs, numbered steps, and tables organize information where useful.
  • GEO-008 Terms, entity names, units, dates, and product/version details are explicit and unambiguous.
  • GEO-009 Key claims include methodology, assumptions, limitations, and dates where relevant.
  • GEO-010 FAQs address genuine user needs and avoid repetitive or fabricated question-answer blocks.
  • GEO-011 Structured examples or comparisons are accurate and consistent with the surrounding narrative.
  • GEO-040 State prerequisites, limitations, and conditions near short answers where omission would mislead.
  • GEO-041 Ensure charts, figures, and videos have textual context sufficient to convey important facts.
  • GEO-042 Test that extracted answer snippets still make sense without the original page title or navigation.

Authority, provenance, and factual reliability#

  • GEO-012 Claims that could affect decisions are backed by trustworthy, attributable sources.
  • GEO-013 First-party data, original research, real examples, or demonstrated expertise are identified when available.
  • GEO-014 Authors, organizations, editorial responsibility, and update history are stated accurately.
  • GEO-015 Statistics and time-sensitive facts are dated, checked, and scheduled for refresh.
  • GEO-016 Citations and outbound links lead to the actual source and do not imply endorsements.
  • GEO-017 Product names, specifications, organization facts, and public profiles are consistent across owned channels.
  • GEO-043 Maintain a provenance record for changing datasets, prices, statistics, and public statements.
  • GEO-044 Set a review schedule and visible update date for pages with material time-sensitive facts.

Machine readability and discovery#

  • GEO-019 Relevant public pages are crawlable and render essential content in accessible HTML.
  • GEO-020 Canonical URLs, sitemap entries, internal links, and index directives are consistent with the SEO checklist.
  • GEO-021 Schema.org markup is used only where appropriate, valid, and supported by visible page content.
  • GEO-022 Important assets, downloads, and data tables have descriptive text or accessible alternatives.
  • GEO-047 Use provider-published crawler guidance to distinguish search crawling from model-training controls where relevant.
  • GEO-048 Check structured data is consistent with page text and avoid fabricated organization/entity identifiers.

Trustworthy answer experience#

  • GEO-026 Direct answers avoid exaggerated certainty, misleading superlatives, and unsupported comparisons.
  • GEO-027 Policies, pricing, availability, support details, and product limitations are easy to locate and current.
  • GEO-028 Where appropriate, content identifies geographic, regulatory, language, or version differences.
  • GEO-029 Answer snippets preserve context and do not omit material safety, cost, or eligibility caveats.
  • GEO-030 Public contact, entity, and brand information is consistent and can be verified independently.
  • GEO-049 Make sources and important qualifications accessible from short answer sections and summaries.
  • GEO-050 Test quotations and paraphrases for faithful context rather than optimizing only for answer length.
  • GEO-051 Provide explicit correction paths when publicly shared answers or data are found to be wrong. For material inaccuracies in sampled AI-generated brand/product answers (prices, plans, supported platforms, policies, ownership or identity), maintain a dated canonical fact sheet and claim/source log, trace the claim to stale first-party pages, PDFs, feeds or independently cited third-party pages where observable, correct the authoritative source with the responsible owner, and resample actual answers over an appropriate period; do not mark a model answer fixed from one run or promise a two-month convergence deadline.

Measurement and iteration#

  • GEO-031 Baseline questions and evaluation criteria are documented before optimization.

  • GEO-032 For a representative set of real audience questions and relevant competitors, inspect the actual answers and linked sources across chosen AI answer/search systems, retaining model/platform, search mode, location/language if relevant, dates and multiple observations. Treat a repeatedly cited third-party page as a lead for truthful editorial improvement, not a guarantee that outreach or placement will cause future citations.

  • GEO-033 Track sampled AI/search-answer brand mentions, observed linked citations, factual accuracy, crawler requests, referral traffic and conversions as distinct measurements, with source, date, coverage and uncertainty. Bing Webmaster Tools' AI Performance report can provide aggregated, sampled citations and grounding queries across its supported Microsoft/partner experiences, not individual answers, rankings or click counts; its preview Citation Share is contextual and non-causal. Google Search Console's overall Web report, GA4 AI referrers and tool-defined visibility scores are not direct evidence of individual cited answers or AI-wide citation share. Retain actual answer-and-link evidence separately; never equate an observed crawl with a citation.

  • GEO-036 Changes are reviewed for measurable user benefit and aligned with SEO, accessibility, privacy, and legal constraints.

  • GEO-052 Keep a dated, reproducible sample of representative, genuinely asked prompts/questions and observed answer-linked citations, including model/platform, language/locale, retrieval settings, source URLs and repeat-run variation; select a review cadence justified by change risk and sampling cost, not a compulsory number of prompts or weekly rerun.

  • GEO-053 Separate ranking, crawl/index diagnostics, referral logs, answer sampling, and conversions in reports.

  • GEO-079 For public content intended for search and answer discovery, test the live public response for each production hostname, HTTP access, current robots directives (including CDN/edge-managed rules), authentication/WAF challenges and initial versus rendered essential text for Googlebot and each explicitly targeted AI search crawler using current provider documentation. Distinguish search discovery from model-training/grounding policies and user-triggered fetch controls; a spoofed User-Agent in a single curl request, a 200 without usable content or an IP address alone does not authenticate the actual provider bot or establish index/citation eligibility.

  • GEO-080 When organization or product entity identification matters, reconcile the public canonical domain, official name, authorship, organization markup, contact details, and controlled social/business profiles; check for ambiguous names or inconsistent identifiers without claiming search/AI systems require a custom domain or guarantee entity recognition.

Frontend Checks#

Apply to browser-based, mobile-web, embedded, or other user-facing interfaces. Record N/A with reasons for headless services.

Reference basis: Google Search Central — AI features and your website; Google Search Central — Guide to optimizing for generative AI features; Google Search Central — JavaScript SEO basics.

  • GEO-066 Put a direct, accurate answer near the relevant question while retaining context and meaningful caveats.
  • GEO-067 Use descriptive headings, semantic HTML, tables, and lists that remain understandable without interactive widgets.
  • GEO-068 Expose primary facts in rendered textual content; give charts, images, and media adequate text alternatives.
  • GEO-069 Use stable public URLs and standard anchor links to canonical source pages.
  • GEO-070 Verify initial HTML/rendered output shows the essential content to intended crawlers, including JavaScript-based pages.
  • GEO-071 Match visible headings, answers, dates, and entities to supported structured data without invisible or invented claims.
  • GEO-072 Present citations and source links where a reader can inspect supporting primary information.
  • GEO-073 Avoid misleading summaries, unsupported numerical claims, or fabricated quotes in callouts and snippets.
  • GEO-074 State geographic scope, eligibility, currency, date, and relevant version in comparative answer sections.
  • GEO-075 Test mobile layout, accessibility, readability, and critical interactions so sources are usable by humans.
  • GEO-076 Check translated or region-specific pages keep facts, named entities, and caveats consistent across languages.
  • GEO-077 Confirm outdated or deleted content results in a clear correction/redirect or appropriate missing-page status.
  • GEO-078 Make public contact, organization, product, and publication details consistent across page templates.

SEO and GEO launch factors — evidence and limits#

Use the checks above and the related SEO/launch files to evaluate the following factors; importance labels are practical triage guidance, not official search-engine weights or proven ranking factors.

Factor Practical priority Basis
Public content crawlable by intended search and AI-search systems Critical when public discovery is a goal Test robots, HTTP, auth, CDN, links and rendered output; a provider may use distinct crawlers for search, training or user-requested fetches
Original, relevant, accurate, useful information Critical Prioritize factual usefulness and verifiable firsthand or authoritative information, not content written solely for algorithmic inclusion
Accessible textual HTML and clear page structure High Use useful headings, descriptive anchors, and important text visible without special interaction
Credible authors, source citations and consistent public entity information High Identify the actual organization/author; allow readers to verify claims; consistency helps avoid confusion but cannot guarantee AI recognition
Structured data consistent with the visible page Useful where applicable Use supported types and real entity identifiers; no special AI-only schema is required for Google Search
Controlled custom domain versus github.io / pages.dev hostname Operational/brand decision A controlled domain aids portability and stable identity, not an independently established direct ranking bonus
Organic mentions and relevant editorial links Context-dependent Earn real references through useful content and legitimate outreach; avoid link schemes

Release gate#

  • All applicable high-priority checks above pass, or an authorized decision-maker has explicitly accepted and documented each residual risk.
  • Failed items have tracked remediation, owners, and deadlines; material blockers remain blocked until resolved.
  • Evidence links and the reviewer, review date, and final decision are recorded.

Domain-specific approval rule: Do not approve deceptive, fabricated, or unsubstantiated content. Verify essential public facts and make evidence available; AI answer visibility cannot be promised.

Trusted references and scope#

The checks above are adapted into practical verification questions from these authoritative publications (not copied as standards text). Verify current versions and the project's scope before sign-off.

  • Google Search Central — AI features and your website
  • Google Search Central — Guide to optimizing for generative AI features
  • Google Search Central — JavaScript SEO basics
  • Google Search Central — Structured data introduction
  • OpenAPI Specification 3.2.1
  • NIST — Generative AI Risk Management Profile

GEO/AEO techniques are not separate eligibility requirements for Google AI Overviews or AI Mode. Google documents ordinary Search eligibility, helpful content, and no required AI-specific markup. Other providers differ; inclusion and citations are not guaranteed.

  • Google Search Central — AI features and your website — ordinary Search eligibility, crawlable text, visible-content/structured-data consistency, and AI-feature traffic included in Search Console's aggregated Web search reporting.

  • Google Search Central — AI optimization guide — llms.txt is not used by Google Search, including AI features.

  • Google — Overview of crawlers and fetchers — crawler and user-triggered fetcher distinctions.

  • Bing Webmaster Tools — AI Performance — sampled citation, grounding-query, trend and optional citation-share preview data, not rankings or click counts.

  • Bing Webmaster Blog — AI visibility preview — provenance and limits of Citation Share/Compare.

  • OpenAI — Overview of OpenAI crawlers — distinguish OAI-SearchBot, GPTBot, and ChatGPT-User where applicable.

  • Google — Google-Extended crawler control — product token, not separate HTTP crawler; different from Googlebot's Search role.

  • OpenAI — Crawlers and user agents — OAI-SearchBot supports search; GPTBot concerns model training; ChatGPT-User is user-triggered.

  • Cloudflare — Bot Fight Mode — potential edge challenges; inspect actual events and delivered content.

Source review date: 2026-11-13. Targeted citation/referral measurement verification: 2026-11-14 (Google AI-features documentation and upstream provider descriptions).

Suggested testing tools#

Choose tools appropriate to the project's stack and risks; automation supports evidence but does not approve the checklist.

  • Test focus: machine-readable answers, structured data, citation links, and content consistency (not rankings); include browser and client behavior where applicable.
  • Cross-stack: Schema.org Validator + lychee.
  • Python: Beautiful Soup + pytest; for pytest-based suites, run python -m pytest -q.
  • TypeScript: Playwright + schema-dts + Vitest; for Vitest-based suites, run npx vitest run (or npx playwright test for E2E).
  • JavaScript: Playwright + Ajv + Jest; for Jest-based suites, run npx jest --ci (or npx playwright test for E2E).
  • Optional AI-answer visibility research platforms (upstream reviewed 2026-11-14; not required or independently benchmarked): NiubiGEO offers self-hosted multi-model brand and competitor prompt research with saved original responses/citations, repeatable observations, dated comparison and keyword monitoring (some monitoring features are beta). Keep explicit model/search settings and baseline prompts, export answer/link evidence, capture failed runs, and protect API keys; self-hosting does not eliminate external model-API disclosure or provider/hosting charges. OpenSEO also provides optional SEO and AI-visibility research with agent plugin skills; its self-hosted data features can require paid DataForSEO and additional APIs. Secure/claim the initial admin before any public exposure. For either product, map results to GEO-031–033/052/053; do not confuse tool-derived scores, brand mentions or referral analytics with independently observed AI citation links.
  • Optional answer-source research: With a responsible owner's permission, sample authentic buyer questions across selected AI answer tools; retain observed answers, dated source URLs and changing results before proposing original data, helpful comparisons, corrections, publisher outreach or genuine review profiles. An independent editor may decline a pitch, no platform is obligated to cite the page, and citation share requires a defined provider/query/timeframe denominator. When available, compare separately with Bing Webmaster Tools AI Performance (aggregate cited pages and preview Citation Share) and Search Console Web search/analytics (clicks/impressions, not an isolated Google AI citation report). Do not equate log fetches, backlinks or GA4 referrers with AI answer links; see GEO-031–033/052/053.
  • Optional RomeoSEO GEO/AI-agent skills (source paths verified 2026-11-14, not installed): ai-agent-readiness, ai-prompt-research, ai-brand-facts and ai-traffic-analytics can inform GEO-031–033/047/051–053/079–081 as reviewer aids. Pin and inspect instructions, scripts, connector scope, data recipients and costs before use. Independently validate actual source URLs, dated answer samples and brand facts; avoid confusing a model's hidden searches, GSC impressions, crawler hits, traffic attribution, Bing AI Performance aggregate citations and an observed answer's linked citation.
  • AI-answer citation opportunity register: Build a small, dated set of real customer questions; record the answer, displayed brand names, direct cited URLs, provider/model, relevant language/locale and repeats. Group cited sources as independent buyer guides, review directories, forums, videos and official websites. Where a third-party page is genuinely missing a tested product fact, original dataset or meaningful alternative, contact its editor with the supporting evidence and respect their choice. Treat published mentions, linked AI citations, crawls and conversions as distinct observations. Maps to GEO-001/031/032/033/052/053 and SEO-082.
  • Brand-fact and practical answer upkeep: Maintain a dated canonical product reference (features, supported platforms, current plans/prices, availability and limits) and test representative answers against it. For a discrepancy, preserve the quoted answer and linked source if visible, correct your own authoritative pages or send a documented correction request to independent publishers, then resample the relevant questions. Use source-complete short answers and appropriate accessible comparison tables/videos, without fixed 40–80-word, 20-prompt or two-month thresholds. Maps to GEO-006/013/027/042/043/044/051/052.
  • Search-access diagnostics from owned telemetry: For explicitly targeted AI search crawlers, compare live robots and WAF/CDN policy with aggregated permitted edge/origin logs, meaningful HTTP status/blocked-event reasons and delivered HTML. Keep search crawler traffic separate from training bots and user-triggered requests; when a key public page has no visible requests, also check the logging window and crawler identity before changing the site. Maps to GEO-047/079/081, SEO-013/086.
  • Evidence: Save tool versions, configuration, test environment, fixtures, results, and links in project-specific review records using the existing checklist IDs. Expert review remains necessary where relevant.

Suggested AI skills for verification#

These are optional agent review aids, not automated passes or release approval. Listed repository popularity was checked on 2026-11-12; these skills were not installed or executed. Star counts and security badges do not establish correctness or safety; inspect code and permissions before use.

  • ai-seo — Review answer-engine discoverability and source quality (coreyhaines31/marketingskills, 59,899 repo stars).
  • schema — Check machine-readable content structure (coreyhaines31/marketingskills, 59,899 repo stars).
  • seo-audit — Identify crawl and citation-link issues (coreyhaines31/marketingskills, 59,899 repo stars).

Additional optional marketing-agent role templates (upstream reviewed 2026-11-14; not installed or autonomous tests): Agency Agents' marketing division includes an AI Citation Strategist, AEO Foundations Architect, and Agentic Search Optimizer. Use these as editable research prompts, not verification results. Check observed answers, citation links, permissions, consent and source validity against GEO-031–033/047/052/053/079. The templates discuss optional llms.txt, agent-facing discovery files and experimental WebMCP: none is a required Google AI Search signal or guaranteed browser/agent integration. WebMCP remains experimental; independently test target browsers and authorize all consequential actions.

How to check: In a project-specific copy, have the agent audit the frontend scope and map findings to this file's existing checklist IDs, with code/configuration references, reproducible test results, failed or inapplicable cases, and uncertainties. Independently verify findings; keep shared template boxes unchecked and retain human approval requirements.

Before use: Read the skill's SKILL.md, referenced scripts, license, and requested tool permissions. Only execute vetted skills with appropriate access in a controlled environment.

Important warning: reference only#

⚠️ Reference only — not a definitive or exhaustive checklist. This template is a starting point for review, not the ultimate authority or a guarantee of project safety, quality, regulatory compliance, accessibility, security, or launch readiness.

Use project-specific judgment and independent verification. Requirements and risks evolve and differ by project, technology, and jurisdiction. Adapt the checks, consult current authoritative sources, perform relevant tests, and obtain qualified specialist review or approval when appropriate. Checking every box does not replace these steps.

Reference, not a certification. Check applicability, verify important claims against current primary sources, and seek expert review where necessary. Suggest an improvement.
